surfaceNarrative.concept: Portable archive is a framework-owned backup/export/import/restore contract surfaced through Clawix Settings/Data with signed-host handling for secrets and human confirmation.

completingSurface.human: Clawix Settings/Data portable archive export, verify, import preview, restore and restore report UI.
completingSurface.programmatic: claw archive plan|export|verify|inspect|import|restore|doctor --json and ClawJS PortableArchive* contracts.

surfaceNarrative.nonInference: This surface does not make Clawix the archive schema steward, authorize plaintext secret export, or bypass signed-host approval for restore-sensitive paths.

resourceContract.startup: Portable archive UI does not start archive work at app launch; it reads status only when the Settings/Data surface is opened or an explicit archive action is requested.
resourceContract.idle: Idle state retains only bounded UI status and no active export/import worker, file watcher, or polling loop.
resourceContract.memory: Archive previews and reports must stay summarized in UI state; large payloads stream through framework/host contracts instead of full in-memory mirrors.
resourceContract.streaming: Long export/import/verify/restore progress uses cancellable, bounded progress events with route-specific backpressure and no unbounded UI fanout.
resourceContract.storage: Portable archive files live under the user-selected archive/export destinations and framework contracts; Clawix stores only host-operational status and approval state.
resourceContract.hotPath: Settings navigation and archive status rendering must remain metadata-only and avoid scanning archive contents on the UI hot path.
resourceContract.scale: Archive item enumeration must use framework previews, windows, or summaries; whole-archive reads require explicit bounded contract evidence.
resourceContract.validation: PortableArchiveSettingsTests, portable_archive_mirror_check.mjs, surface_resource_contract_guard.mjs, and sibling ClawJS portable archive governance check

surfaceNarrative.concept: OpenCode is a framework-owned runtime adapter choice surfaced in Clawix only when the feature flag marks the adapter visible.

surfaceNarrative.nonInference: This interface surface does not make Clawix the runtime adapter steward, bypass framework registry policy, or enable hidden adapters without the feature flag.

resourceContract.startup: The selector does not start an adapter on launch; it reads visible runtime adapter metadata when the settings/runtime surface is shown.
resourceContract.idle: Idle state keeps only selected adapter metadata and feature visibility, not a running adapter process.
resourceContract.memory: The adapter list is bounded by the framework runtime adapter registry and rendered as a small selector model.
resourceContract.streaming: No stream is owned by the selector; active runtime job streams must declare their own route resource contracts.
resourceContract.storage: Selection persists through framework runtime configuration or host policy, not a separate Clawix-owned runtime store.
resourceContract.hotPath: UI routing and selector rendering are the hot path and must remain simple metadata reads.
resourceContract.scale: Designed for tens of adapters; 1,000 entries require searchable/paginated selection, and 100,000 adapters are outside product scope.
resourceContract.validation: node scripts/surface_resource_contract_guard.mjs and Runtime adapter registry tests

surfaceNarrative.nonInference: This surface does not promote experimental composer behavior to default visibility or change the framework message contract without its own route decision.

resourceContract.startup: Composer experiment state is read with the composer and does not start background work on launch.
resourceContract.idle: Idle state keeps only feature visibility and draft UI state; no timer, poller, or worker is owned here.
resourceContract.memory: State is bounded to the active composer draft and small feature metadata.
resourceContract.streaming: Message streaming remains owned by the chat/message pipeline, not this feature gate.
resourceContract.storage: Draft state remains host UI state while durable message data follows the framework message contract.
resourceContract.hotPath: Composer rendering reads the feature flag and avoids heavy derivation in the body.
resourceContract.scale: Designed for a small set of composer controls; larger experiment catalogs require a separate paged registry.
resourceContract.validation: node scripts/surface_narrative_guard.mjs, node scripts/surface_resource_contract_guard.mjs, and composer visibility tests

resourceContract.startup: Tool UI does not execute tools on launch; it renders existing timeline metadata when a message is visible.
resourceContract.idle: Idle state retains bounded presentation state and no polling or execution worker.
resourceContract.memory: Tool groups are bounded by visible message/timeline presentation and bridge fixture contracts.
resourceContract.streaming: Streaming tool updates flow through the existing message stream with coalesced presentation updates.
resourceContract.storage: Durable tool records remain in framework session/message storage; host policy stores only approval settings.
resourceContract.hotPath: Visible tool row rendering consumes precomputed presentation models.
resourceContract.scale: Designed for visible timeline groups; large histories require transcript windowing before rendering.

resourceContract.startup: Network Control is route-demanded and does not start connector work while hidden.
resourceContract.idle: Idle state keeps only feature visibility and last visible route status; background connector work must declare its own inventory.
resourceContract.memory: Rendered state is bounded to the visible connector/network summary.
resourceContract.streaming: Connector updates must use route-owned bounded streams or snapshots.
resourceContract.storage: Connector state remains framework-owned with host policy references for sensitive actions.
resourceContract.hotPath: Sidebar and command visibility checks are simple feature-flag reads.
resourceContract.scale: Designed for visible connector summaries; large connector sets require search or pagination.
resourceContract.validation: Surface route registry checks, node scripts/surface_narrative_guard.mjs, and node scripts/surface_resource_contract_guard.mjs

surfaceNarrative.concept: Runtime ecosystem lens scopes Clawix to one native runtime while preserving provenance, freshness, field/action authority, and local-only overlays.

authorizingDecision.ref: ADR 0033 runtime ecosystem integration standard mirror

completingSurface.human: Filtered runtime lens views for sessions, skills, memory, channels, providers, settings, and diagnostics.
completingSurface.programmatic: ClawJS runtime ecosystem manifest and claw runtime <runtime-id> portal.

surfaceNarrative.nonInference: This dev-only registry row does not claim full UI parity, live runtime validation, or write-back support.

resourceContract.startup: No runtime ecosystem scan at Clawix launch.
resourceContract.idle: No watcher or polling loop unless a runtime lens/sync contract is active.
resourceContract.memory: Large native runtime lists stay windowed or summarized.
resourceContract.streaming: Runtime events use bounded bridge streams.
resourceContract.storage: Clawix stores host/UI state and explicit local overlays, not runtime truth.
resourceContract.scale: Session, memory, skill, log and diagnostic lists need limits or cursors.
